A_target.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be points on a [[Definition:Circle|circle]] such that $AB$ is a [[Definition:Diameter of Circle|diameter]].
Then $\angle ACB$ is a [[Definition:Right Angle|right angle]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\angle APB$ be an [[Definition:Inscribed Angle|inscribed angle]] of a circle with center $O$.
Then $\angle APB = \dfrac 1 2 \angle AOB$, where $\angle AOB$ is the central angle on the same arc.

object_map.reformulation: Specialize the inscribed angle theorem to a chord through the center.

validity_conditions: The center O lies on AB, so the central angle on the arc not containing C is 180 degrees.
The converse also holds: a right angle at C places C on the circle with diameter AB.
proof_plan: As $AB$ is a diameter, the center $O$ is the [[Definition:Midpoint|midpoint]] of $AB$, and $\angle AOB$ is a straight angle of $180 \degrees$.
$\angle ACB$ is an inscribed angle subtending the arc $AB$ not containing $C$.
